terminal_reading: The job asks for a prospectively frozen prediction TOURNAMENT over held-out families. A tournament requires someone other than the predictor to hold the outcomes until predictions are locked. In this session I would be both predictor and custodian, and splitting data while promising not to look is not custody -- it is the predictor holding the answers. The terminal was frozen before the work below and stands regardless of it.

structural_verification.detail: T23's decidable content holds over a total enumeration of 100 cells with zero violations: ScientificAdvance is exactly Available AND Admit. Both independence countermodels the theorem names are present -- 25 reachable-but-unauthorized cells and 25 well-specified-but-unreachable cells -- so independence is witnessed in both directions rather than assumed. A grid containing only one would not witness it.

impossibility_clauses.detail: T23 says more compute cannot replace missing authority and stronger governance cannot manufacture unreachable methods. Raising compute to maximum produced an advance in ZERO cells where Admit was false; raising governance to maximum produced an advance in ZERO cells where Available was false. These are the two clauses that make the coupling a constraint rather than a definition.

what_this_does_not_establish: This is NOT the tournament. No prediction was made, nothing was held out, and no outcome was concealed from the predictor.
Structural verification of a biconditional is not prospective evidence. T23 could be structurally sound and still fail to predict anything about held-out families.
The enumeration is complete but self-authored. Not external adjudication.
what_would_discharge_this_job: A third party holding outcomes for held-out families while predictions are registered. Free routes exist: OSF preregistration timestamps a prediction before outcomes are accessible, and a public leaderboard with server-side labels supplies custody the predictor does not control. Neither was used here.
